title: Penetration Testing for Web, API and AI Applications | utxo AG
description: Recurring penetration tests by utxo AG for web applications, APIs, infrastructure and AI applications: report, remediation and retest.
tagline: Recurring penetration tests for web applications, APIs, infrastructure and AI
lede: We test your systems the way an attacker would approach them, and we repeat it at regular intervals. Every round ends with a report, fixed vulnerabilities and a retest.

faq.a: That depends on your systems, your release rhythm and your requirements. We agree the interval with you. After larger changes, an additional round is advisable.

faq.q: Does a penetration test find every vulnerability?
faq.a: No. A test shows which vulnerabilities were found within the agreed scope and the available time. It is a snapshot and not proof that a system is free of gaps. This is one reason why we test regularly and again after changes.

faq.q: Do you also test production systems?
faq.a: Yes, if you want us to. We agree with you in advance which tests run on the production system, in which time window and with which restrictions.

faq.q: What do you need from us to start?
faq.a: Written authorization from the system owner, a description of the systems in scope, contacts in your IT and, depending on the type of test, test accounts. Systems hosted by third parties, such as a hosting provider, also require their consent.
Only the people you name. We treat findings and reports as confidential and do not pass them on to third parties.

faq.q: Do you also test AI applications and agents?
faq.a: Yes. We develop AI applications and agents ourselves and test them like any other application. This includes, for example, whether an agent can be led to take actions it is not allowed to take, or whether it discloses data a person has no access to.

scope.title: What you get
scope.text: Penetration tests for an agreed scope, repeated at the agreed interval and after larger changes. We test with current tools and according to current standards, and we keep both up to date.

points.name: Systems tested
points.text: Web applications, interfaces and APIs, infrastructure, and AI applications and agents. We define the scope with you before every round.

points.name: Report
points.text: Every finding is described, rated by risk and comes with a concrete recommendation. A summary for management comes first.

points.name: Remediation
points.text: We explain the findings to your development and IT teams and support them with the fix.

points.name: Retest
points.text: Once the vulnerabilities are fixed, we test them again and record what is closed.

points.name: Next round
points.text: The next round follows at the agreed interval or after a major release. This keeps your security level traceable over time.

report.label: Animated sample view of a test report: four findings are shown in turn, each with its risk rating, description and recommendation. Sample data.

findings.title: Access control can be bypassed
findings.description: Signed-in users can retrieve other customers' orders.
findings.advice: Check authorization on the server for every request.

findings.title: Account with excessive privileges
findings.description: The application's account may change more data than it needs.
findings.advice: Restrict the account's privileges to what is necessary.

findings.title: Session does not expire
findings.advice: End sessions on sign-out and limit their lifetime.

findings.title: Outdated library
findings.description: A component in use is not up to date.
findings.advice: Update the component and check dependencies continuously.

example.title: One finding as an example
example.text: A retail company has its customer portal tested regularly. In round 4, the API turns out to let signed-in users retrieve other customers' orders. A second finding carries a low risk. What happens with it is the company's decision.

finding.label: Animated sample view: two findings are rated by risk. The critical one is reported, fixed and retested after your approval. For the second one, the company accepts the residual risk until the next release.

project.title: How we work together
project.text: It starts with a conversation about your systems and your goals. After that, every test round follows the same sequence. How often we test is agreed with you: it depends on your systems and your release rhythm.

steps.name: Scope and authorization
steps.text: We define with you which systems are tested, how deeply and in which time windows. Testing only takes place with written authorization from the system owner.

steps.name: Test
steps.text: We test the agreed systems from an attacker's point of view, with current tools and by hand. We report critical findings immediately.

steps.name: Report
steps.text: You receive all findings with a risk rating and a recommendation. We walk your team through the report.

steps.name: Remediation
steps.text: Your team or your service provider fixes the vulnerabilities. We answer questions and support the implementation.

steps.name: Retest and next round
steps.text: We test the fixed findings again. The next round follows at the agreed interval or after larger changes.

rounds.label: Animated diagram with sample data: six test rounds over time. The number of findings falls from round to round, and new ones appear after a major release. Almost all are closed after the retest.
rounds.title: Findings per test round

legend.open: open, carried into the next round

organisation.title: Coordination with your organization
organisation.text: A penetration test touches live operations. That is why it is settled in advance who is informed, when testing takes place and who decides. The results are confidential.

points.name: Contacts
points.text: Your IT and utxo AG each name one contact. They coordinate the test windows and can be reached during the test.

points.name: Test windows
points.text: You decide when testing takes place, for example outside business hours or ahead of a release.

points.name: Production or test system
points.text: We clarify with you what is tested on the test system and what is necessary on the production system. Tests that carry a risk for operations only run after your approval.

points.name: Confidentiality
points.text: Findings and reports only go to the agreed group of recipients. You determine who sees the report.

points.name: Your decision
points.text: You decide what happens with a finding: fix it, schedule it or deliberately accept a residual risk.
